A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same SciRM/SciRM-Ref research. Their complete main texts and appendices are readable, and equations, experiments, figures and tables can be matched across renumbering and relocation.

before.justification: Section 5 and Appendix D report original evaluation results across four scientific-writing tasks, including unseen-task and unseen-aspect experiments.

after.justification: v2 retains these original results and adds GPT-5.2 comparisons, F1 scores, reasoning ablations and qualitative reasoning-trace analyses.

M1.justification: The Qwen2.5-based models, two-stage GRPO procedure, reward functions, length penalty and reflection process remain unchanged. The reasoning-disabled variant is introduced only as an evaluation control.

E1.justification: Both versions train on related-work evaluation and RevUtil, evaluate unseen novelty-alignment and scientific-revision tasks, and retain the same held-out Actionability/Grounding scenario. The new analyses use existing task coverage.

E2.justification: GPT-5.2 (2025-12-11) is added to comparisons across all four tasks, including Figures 3–4 and Tables 1–2. Existing comparators remain; Granite/Granite3.3 and Llama/Llama3.1 are label refinements for the same specified models.

E3.justification: v2 adds F1 alongside accuracy and introduces an inference control that removes reasoning instructions and example reasoning from prompts (Section 6.2). Existing dataset splits, model configurations and ordinary inference sampling settings remain unchanged.

E4.justification: v2 retains the masked-aspect experiment and substantially expands component and error analyses. Section 6 adds reasoning-removal ablations for both models across all four tasks, while Appendix E supplies comparative actionability, novelty and revision traces. These directly investigate the claimed role of reasoning beyond v1's brief error discussion.

E5.justification: Both versions report means and standard deviations over five inference repetitions, with three for proprietary evaluators. v2 applies the existing three-run convention to GPT-5.2 and the existing uncertainty-reporting practice to F1 results; retained experiments' run counts and statistical procedures are unchanged.

E6.justification: v2 adds GPT-5.2 scores, F1 results across all tasks and reasoning-ablation results. Table 4 reports novelty-accuracy drops of 0.21 for SciRM and 0.25 for SciRM-Ref. Table 11 newly reports related-work F1 of 0.89 for GPT-5.2 versus 0.87 for SciRM-Ref. Retained accuracies are otherwise unchanged except o3-mini's overall revision accuracy, corrected from 0.83 in v1 Table 8 to 0.84 in v2 Table 10.

T1.justification: Section 3.2 retains the same task definitions, piecewise scoring reward, length-penalty formula and reflection reward. No mathematical assumptions, derivations or proofs are added or substantively revised.

C1.justification: The abstract, introduction's contributions and findings, and conclusion retain the same claims about two-stage training, rubric-conditioned reasoning, multi-aspect evaluation and cross-task generalization. New evidence supports existing contributions.

C2.justification: Sections 5–6 more explicitly interpret performance as transferable reasoning rather than memorization and explain improvements through rubric alignment and attention to textual details. v1's discussion of RevUtil annotator disagreement and adjacent-score confusion is removed. The dedicated Limitations section remains unchanged.

D1.justification: The code reference changes to UKPLab/acl2026-expert-rm, with matching displayed text and embedded destination; v1's displayed repository name differed from its link. The data destination, LoRA rank, hardware, training time, sampling details and full evaluation prompts remain unchanged.

R1.justification: The ARR Reviewer Guidelines citation accompanying v1's novelty-error discussion is removed. Research positioning otherwise remains stable. Changes such as DeepSeek-R1's publication entry and RewardBench 2/RewardEval match existing works rather than introducing new research sources.

P1.justification: The brief error-analysis paragraph is replaced by a dedicated Model Analysis and Ablation Studies section, and Appendix E is added. Other changes include localized wording edits, clearer model labels, affiliations and revised acknowledgments; most existing prose and section order remain intact.

P2.justification: v2 substantially expands evidence displays with reasoning-summary and ablation tables, three F1 tables and three full side-by-side reasoning-trace tables. Figures 3–4 add GPT-5.2 bars and revise colors and legends. Existing tables and prompt figures move or are renumbered, with prompt contents preserved.

improvement.justification: The reasoning ablation and inspectable traces strengthen evidence for the existing reasoning claims, while GPT-5.2 comparisons and F1 results broaden empirical scrutiny. The revision also corrects an appendix accuracy inconsistency. These benefits are tempered by the unspecified scope of the manual trace analysis and removal of the annotator-disagreement caveat, yielding a limited overall improvement.
